## F214 post-deploy audit — first hour

Deployed merge: `a70cace40b002e9940b230b5ca27d6763a72977c`; `PAST_TTL = Warn` (b). PID `36530` reported that revision at both deployment verification and the end-window check. This audit was run by PERFORMANCE only.

### Windows and method

- **Before (B):** 2026-11-12 03:36:05.250Z–2026-11-19 03:36:05.250Z; 14,620 delivered, 13,404 paired, 9,402 decided.
- **After (A):** 2026-11-19 05:08:00Z–06:10:00Z, 62 minutes; 261 delivered, 233 paired, 151 decided. Of the paired deliveries, 76 were busy and six were non-busy partial-cache cases, excluded from decided counts. Fleet report: 1,507 calls, 307 turns, 54 sessions, 14 unseated.
- Same audit pairing and thresholds: previous/next main-chain calls, next call within 15 minutes, cache-read share ≥50% warm / <10% cold. B uses the pre-F214 guard; A uses shipped Warn. Counts below are reconstructed **guard decisions over delivered-call pairs**, not observed sender refusals. Window lengths and traffic differ; do not infer rates or significance from raw totals. `—` means no decided after samples, not proof of zero risk.

### Per harness × model × route

### What this window establishes—and does not

- No decided large cold 5-minute-TTL case occurred after deployment. The one modeled warm warning was plain Copilot Claude at 6.37 minutes idle, with a 99.8% next-call cache-read share. This exercises the Warn classification, not demonstrated prevention of an expensive cold wake.
- The remaining modeled large cold allow was proxied Claude: approximately 26 minutes idle on a native one-hour TTL; next-call cache-read share 8.6%. A TTL is not a guarantee of actual cache residency.
- Recounting all after rows independently yielded zero `new_guard` mismatches. The two modeled refusals were delivered pairs, not proof of two rejected requests. There were no `send.cold-wake-forced`, `watchdog.nudge`, or `watchdog.idle-nudge` events in the window. Ordinary-send `cold_check` is attached to the response after delivery-outcome persistence; those spine events do not prove that the server issued the modeled warning. Context availability after a daemon restart is another replay-vs-runtime limit. No actual refusal-error rate or avoided-token savings is claimed.
- The report window can omit a pre-window predecessor for Claude/OMP; pairs without both required calls are excluded. This first-hour sample does not replace a longitudinal effectiveness study.

### Deployed surface and resource receipts

Live `pij-rs state` output at 05:09Z showed Copilot GPT `cache 30m native`, plain Copilot Claude `cache 5m native`, and proxied Claude `cache 1h proxy`. No synthetic wake was induced.

| Launch measurement | Before merge | After deployment |
|---|---:|---:|
| Measured interval | 20.3384 s | 20.5094 s |
| Daemon total counters | 1763 → 1763 | 571 → 581 |
| Daemon launch delta | 0 | 10, all existing `ps.registration-native-process` |
| Whole-machine launches/s | 284.6 | 148.1 |

All other after-window launch-site deltas were zero. There is no new TTL launch site; the measured fleet did **not** have zero launches. Different fleet activity and the restart prevent attributing the machine-rate difference to F214. After pair: 05:09:33.189Z–05:09:53.698Z. Daemon CPU/RSS snapshots were 16.9% / 111,504 KiB near deployment and 13.6% / 145,744 KiB at 06:10:44Z; these are not isolated CPU or leak measurements.

The audit itself exited 0: 2.26 s wall, 1.69 s user + 0.45 s system, maximum RSS 82,198,528 bytes, zero swaps. Report folding used two threads at nice 19; the audit recipe also runs at nice 19. No local builds or tests.

Reproduction (local reports are not published):
```sh
nice -n 19 pij-rs fleet-report "$HOME" --since 2026-11-19T05:08:00Z --until 2026-11-19T06:10:00Z --threads 2 --out /tmp/f214/fr-after-a70cace4-0610
just cache-ttl-audit /tmp/f214/fr-after-a70cace4-0610
```

Audit-tool provenance: `70d01ba27a6258efa69b66d30ba5671ee1d30b68`, script SHA-256 `9dafb2b618980a7833c3748d45925ababe0fadd27a02c5e97a0a0a4557cf74e5`. The tool changed during the scheduled wait to correct legacy `cache_*` diagnostics; its guard/policy computation is unchanged from the merged review. The deployed daemon stayed at the merge SHA above. Only guard metrics are compared here.
